entries.name:
guideline: Single vs. multiple expansion.

By default, only

fields.before: An accordion displays a list of items that can be expanded or collapsed to show additional content. It can support zero, one, or multiple expanded items at a time.
fields.after:
Single vs. multiple expansion.

By default, only one accordion item may be expanded at a time. However, the component can be configured to allow multiple items to remain open simultaneously.

entries.name:
guideline: Title wrapping.

Accordion titles wrap automatic

fields.before: By default, only one accordion item can be expanded at a time. Use the isMultiple option to allow multiple items to be expanded simultaneously.
fields.after:
Title wrapping.

Accordion titles wrap automatically if they exceed the available width.

entries.name:
guideline: Optional actions.

An optional action button or

fields.before: Accordions can contain any number of items. Each item can be expanded or collapsed by interacting with any part of the item.
fields.after:
Optional actions.

An optional action button or switch can be placed on the trailing edge of an accordion item to support contextual interactions.

entries.name:
guideline: Progressive disclosure.

Accordions are effectiv

fields.before: Accordions come in three densities: compact, regular, and spacious. Each of the different densities have the same font size, but have tighter or looser vertical spacing between the rows.
fields.after:
Progressive disclosure.

Accordions are effective for organizing large amounts of related content within a limited space. They help users stay focused by revealing information only when it's needed, making them ideal for scenarios where not all content needs to be visible at once.

entries.name: guideline: Individual accordion items can be disabled using

before.content: Individual accordion items can be disabled using the isDisabled option. Disabled items cannot be expanded or collapsed.

entries.name: guideline: By default, accordions have dividers between sec

before.content: By default, accordions have dividers between sections. This style works best when lots of content is inside each section.

entries.name: guideline: Alternatively, you can have no dividers between

before.content: Alternatively, you can have no dividers between sections. This style works best when a clear layout (vertical stack, table, grid) makes it easy see and understand. Too many quiet components in a small space can be hard to differentiate.

entries.name: guideline: Accordions come in four different sizes: small,

before.content: Accordions come in four different sizes: small, medium, large, and extra-large. The medium size is the default and recommended option. Use the other sizes sparingly; they should be used to create a hierarchy of importance within the page. Each of the different sizes have varying font sizes, and tighter or looser vertical spacing between the rows.

before.content: Avoid using accordions when users are likely to read all the content in one go, as they can introduce unnecessary clicks and hinder the user experience. after.description: Whether the rendered accordion item is expanded. Drives the chevron direction and the content area. Per-item expansion in a data-driven accordion is items[].isExpanded.

after.name: content
after.description: Area below the header holding the item's content. Shown only while the item is open (isOpen).

after.name: disclosure-icon
after.description: Chevron at the start of the header. It points to the end while the item is closed and down while it is open.

after.name: divider
after.description: One-pixel line below the item. Absent when the accordion is quiet (isQuiet).

after.name: header
after.description: Row holding the disclosure icon and the title. It is the interactive heading.

after.name: item
after.description: One accordion item: a header, the content area while open, and the divider below.

after.name: title
